sections.title: Form and identification
sections.text: Prunus spinosa, the blackthorn, is a suckering deciduous shrub or small tree usually up to about 4 m tall. Its dark branches bear rigid thorns; the white flowers, about 1.5 cm across, commonly open before the leaves.

sections.title: Leaves and sloes
sections.text: The small, toothed leaves follow flowering. The round blue-black fruits, called sloes, are about 1 cm across and have a pale waxy bloom and a single stone.

sections.title: Food and related cherries
sections.text: Fresh sloes are edible but strongly astringent; they are more often processed into preserves or drinks. Unlike the sweet cherry (Prunus avium), blackthorn is a thorny shrub with much smaller, astringent fruit.
